corrections.source_phrase: The roots vanishing on T_alpha are the rational multiples of alpha

corrections.reason: A root is a multiplicative character. Vanishing here means the restriction is the identity character, as the immediately preceding display beta|T_alpha=e states. The new Chinese wording preserves this mathematical meaning without implying a character takes value zero.

source_issues_preserved.item: Lemma2.7, definition of d and b
source_issues_preserved.observation: At x_alpha=x_minusalpha=0 the printed d(u)=alpha(t)+x_alpha*x_minusalpha together with b(u)=t*alpha_star(d(u)) gives t*alpha_star(alpha(t)) on T. Conjugation by the Weyl representative in(ii) instead restricts to the reflection t*alpha_star(alpha(t)^(-1)). The rank-one SL2 matrix calculation requires alpha(t)^(-1) in d.
source_issues_preserved.french_verification: Coordinator independently checked French physical PDF pages1309-1310, printed271-272, marginal417-418 and confirmed the same printed d(u)=alpha(t)+x_alpha*x_minusalpha and b(u)=t*alpha_star(d(u)). The French target of d is even printed Spec(Z), whereas the chosen English source has A1. This reviewer did not personally open those French pages.
source_issues_preserved.status: French-confirmed inherited apparent error; rank-one matrix check requires the inverse of alpha(t) in d. Formula retained verbatim.
